title: TokSuite: Measuring the Impact of Tokenizer Choice on Language Model Behavior
claim: The same concept fragments into very different token sequences across tokenizers once real-world perturbations are applied, motivating a controlled benchmark.
layout: Hub-and-spoke grid of 8 dashed perturbation boxes under a central word, colored token chips
description: A central gray box reading "doctor" sits at the top, with a TokSuite logo in the upper left (purple "Tok", yellow "Suite"). Below it, a large dashed container holds a 4x2 grid of smaller dashed panels. The top row covers the translations Turkish, Chinese, Farsi and Italian. The bottom row covers the perturbations OCR Errors, Orth. Errors, Sim. words and Emojis. Each panel shows how four tokenizers split the perturbed word, using rounded token chips: Gemma-2 in yellow, GPT-2 in blue, TokenMonster in green and XGLM in red. A legend of the four colors sits at the top center. The chips show differing fragment counts, such as "d / actor", "phys / ician" and Chinese characters split apart. The Emojis panel shows a face and a staff icon with a "x 13" note. The eye goes first to the "doctor" box, then to the colorful chip grid.
caption: TokSuite is a comprehensive benchmark covering realworld perturbations that change tokenization, and 14 models that share the same initialization, architecture, and data but differ only in their tokenizers. The figure illustrates how different tokenizers fragment the concept “doctor” when subjected to OCR errors, orthographic mistakes, semantic equivalents, emoji substitution, and multilingual translations. Each colored box represents one token across Gemma-2 (yellow), GPT-2 (blue), TokenMonster (green), and XGLM (red) tokenizers.
abstract: Tokenizers provide the fundamental basis through which text is represented and processed by language models (LMs). Despite the importance of tokenization, its role in LM performance and behavior is poorly understood due to the challenge of measuring the impact of tokenization in isolation. To address this need, we present TokSuite, a collection of models and a benchmark that supports research into tokenization's influence on LMs. Specifically, we release fourteen pre-trained models that use different off-the-shelf tokenizers but are otherwise identical, using the same architecture, dataset, training budget, and initialization. We also release a multilingual robustness benchmark that measures model performance under real-world perturbations in English, Chinese, Farsi, Italian, and Turkish, curated by native annotators. Together, TokSuite allows robust decoupling of the influence of a model's tokenizer, supporting a series of novel findings that elucidate the respective benefits and shortcomings of a wide range of popular tokenizers.
